newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Thousands made homeless by Bangladesh floods.
newsitem.headline: Thousands made homeless by Bangladesh floods.

text.p: Floods sweeping Bangladesh's southeastern region have made nearly 100,000 people homeless or stranded in half-submerged houses, officials said on Saturday.
They said the flooding triggered by heavy rain over the past three days had swelled five rivers in the region above danger levels.

"As they are running full to the brim the rivers are likely to burst their banks soon, sending more waters into the devastated areas," said one disaster management official in Chittagong, Bangladesh's main port city.
Separately, 10 fishermen missing in the Bay of Bengal following a rainstorm on Thursday were now believed to have drowned.
"Vessels in the Bay have found some bodies drifting in the rough seas, reinforcing our fears that the missing fishing crew have drowned," one fishing community leader in Cox's Bazar said.
Weather officials said they recorded 98 millimetres of rain in Chittagong in 24 hours to 9.00 a.m. (0300 GMT) on Saturday. The rainfall was heavier in Cox's Bazar, they said.
The deluge began on Thursday in the region as residents were still recovering from last month's floods which killed at least 100 people and made thousands homeless.

Officials said the latest flooding damaged thousands of houses, cut off road communications, threatened train services and swamped crops on 50,000 acres (20,000 hectares) in Chittagong and Cox's Bazar districts. They were unable to give loss estimates immediately.
Roads from Cox's Bazar to Chittagong and Teknaf along the Burmese border have become impassable due to flooding, transport officials said.
Train services between Chittagong and the capital Dhaka might be cut off if rain continued for another two days, they said.
The Bangladesh national airline Biman has reduced flights between Dhaka and Chittagong because of the rains.
Cargo handling at Chittagong port has also been hampered, port officials said.
